key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns inverse design into constrained optimization in a learned latent space, using a generative decoder as a validity prior and a physics-informed optimizer to search for target microstructures.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more feasible design of magnesium alloy microstructures and textures for crystal plasticity-driven property targets without exhaustively querying the expensive simulator.
method: ViT-based encoder compresses EBSD microstructure images into a low-dimensional latent code.
Latent diffusion / diffusion-transformer / rectified-flow decoders reconstruct candidate microstructures with learned validity.
MERIDIAN performs active latent search with deep-kernel GP uncertainty, feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: Trained on about 80,000 EBSD-derived microstructure samples; ViT-FMDiT achieved the best reconstruction quality (FID 27.86, MS-SSIM 0.178) and, within 160 simulations, reduced relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the learned decoder and latent validity model, so out-of-distribution microstructures or solver mismatch could limit optimization reliability.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
